title: Crews of Lancasters ME625 and ND981
memorial_details:
Commemorative display of salvaged aircraft wreckage with associated memorial plaque. The plaque is mounted on a back board within a display case of the remains of the two aircraft, it has a colour badge of 97 Squadron RAF at top centre, and either side are lightly etched depictions of two Lancaster aircraft. The inscription is below with names in two columns by aircraft crew, all etched and in white. Beneath the plaque is a small information panel with brief details of the plaques origin.

The inscription mentions 'UNVEILED BY THE RELATIVES FOR THE 70TH ANNIVERSARY' and the plaque origin information panel states it is an identical copy unveiled near the crash site at Cloot House Farm Crowland.
inscription: Plaque inscription: (97 Squadron badge)/ IN THE SURROUNDING FIELDS LIE THE REMAINS OF LANCASTERS/ ME625 AND ND981 OF 97 SQUADRON RAF BOMBER COMMAND/ WHICH CAME TO REST WITH THEIR CREWS,/ THE RESULT OF A TRAGIC ACCIDENT/ 23RD JUNE 1944/ ME625/ (Names)/ ND981/ (Names)/ UNVEILED BY THE RELATIVES FOR THE 70TH ANNIVERSARY./ PER ARDUA AD ASTRA Plaque origin information panel: This plaque is an identical copy of one unveiled/ near the crash site at Cloot House Farm Crowland.
